in_hebrew.name: אלריקו
in_hebrew.meaning: אל ריקו - האל שלי הוא המלך העשיר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלריקו הוא שם פרטי שמקורו בשפה הגרמנית, אך ניתן לפרש אותו גם בעברית כ'אל ריקו', שפירושו 'האל שלי הוא המלך העשיר'. השם מורכב משני חלקים: 'אל' שפירושו 'אלוהים' ו'ריקו' שפירושו 'מלך עשיר'. השם אלריקו יכול להתפרש כ'האל שלי הוא המלך העשיר והוא השולט על הכל'.

in_greek.name: Αλαρικός
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Αλαρικός είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα, αλλά μπορεί να ερμηνευτεί και στα ελληνικά ως 'ο πλούσιος βασιλιάς'. Το όνομα αποτελείται από δύο μέρη: 'Αλα' που σημαίνει 'αρχή' ή 'αρχικός' και 'ρικός' που σημαίνει 'βασιλιάς' ή 'πλούσιος'. Ο Αλαρικός μπορεί να ερμηνευτεί ως 'ο πλούσιος βασιλιάς που κυβερνά με τη χάρη του Θεού'.

in_latin.name: Alaricus
in_latin.long_meaning: Alaricus est nomen proprium quod originem habet in lingua germanica, sed interpretari potest etiam in lingua latina ut 'dives rex', id est 'rex dives'. Nomen constat ex duabus partibus: 'ala' quod significat 'altus' vel 'potens' et 'ricus' quod significat 'rex' vel 'dives'. Alaricus ergo interpretari potest ut 'rex dives et potens qui regnat cum gratia Dei'.

in_english.name: Alarico
in_english.long_meaning: Alarico is a Christian name derived from Germanic roots, specifically from the Gothic name 'Alaric', which means 'rich ruler' or 'God's ruler'. The name is composed of two elements: 'ala' meaning 'all' or 'foreign' and 'ric' meaning 'ruler' or 'king'. In the context of Christian tradition, Alarico can be interpreted as 'a ruler who is rich in spiritual wealth' or 'one who governs with God's wisdom'. Historically, Alaric I was a king of the Visigoths who sacked Rome in 410 CE. The name Alarico has been used in various Christian cultures and is associated with strength, leadership, and spiritual richness.

data.cultural_impact: Alarico's name holds a significant place in history, as he was the first barbarian king to sack the Eternal City, Rome, in 410 AD. The event marked the decline of the Roman Empire and the beginning of the Middle Ages in Europe. His name has been synonymous with power, conquest, and the fall of Roman rule.
data.spiritual_significance: Alarico's story is a reminder of God's sovereignty over all rulers, which is expressed in the Bible in Daniel 4:17: "This decision is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the word of the most High: it is come unto thee, O king Araxes, by my commandment." The fall of Rome and the rule of Alarico, a Visigoth king, serve as a testament to God's ultimate authority over humanity and empires.
